newsitem.title: USA: Anheuser Busch boosting stake in Mexican brewer.
newsitem.headline: Anheuser Busch boosting stake in Mexican brewer.

text.p: Anheuser-Busch Cos Inc. said Friday it plans to raise its stake in Mexican brewer Grupo Modelo SA de CV again, investing $550 million to boost its holding to 50.2 percent.

Anheuser-Busch, the world's largest brewer, said it expects the $550 million purchase to close sometime later this year. The purchase will bring Anheuser's total investment in Grupo Modelo, the maker of Corona and one of Mexico's leading brewers, to about $1.6 billion.
Anheuser-Busch in May raised its stake in Grupo Modelo and its subsidiaries to 37 percent for $605 million.

The St. Louis-based brewing giant acquired a 17.7 percent interest in Grupo Modelo and its Diblo SA de CV subsidiary in 1993. It had options to increase its investments to 50.2 percent by the end of 1997.
"Our investment in Modelo is a key element in our strategy for international growth," Chairman August Busch III said in a statement.
"Mexico is the seventh largest beer market in the world. With highly favourable demographics and relatively low per-capita consumption, there is signficant growth potential in this market."
Modelo's brands include Corona, Modelo Especial, Pacifico, Negra Modelo and a number of regional brands brewed at eight breweries in Mexico.
Anheuser-Busch holds a 45 percent share of the U.S. beer market.
